name: Random
simple: Random is a random number machine. You make one with Random.new(), then ask it for random whole numbers, random decimals, random directions, or to shuffle a list. If you give it a seed number, it gives the exact same "random" results every time, which is great for things like generating the same map twice.
analogy: Random is like a deck of cards. Random.new() shuffles it in a surprise way. Random.new(42) always shuffles it in the same way, so if you and a friend both use 42, you draw the same cards in the same order.
whenToUse: Rolling dice or picking a random number for loot
Picking a random spawn point or player
Shuffling a list, like the order of mini-games
Making a procedural map that is the same every time for the same seed
where: Works in any script on server or client. Make one with Random.new() or Random.new(seed). Keep it in a variable and reuse it instead of making a new one every time.

terms.pseudorandom: Numbers that look random but are made by a math recipe. With the same starting seed you get the same numbers.
terms.seed: The starting number for the recipe. Same seed = same sequence of results.
terms.integer: A whole number, like 3 or -7, with no decimal part.
terms.inclusive: The end numbers count too. NextInteger(1, 6) can give 1 and can give 6.
terms.unit vector: An arrow with a length of exactly 1. It only says which way, not how far.
terms.shuffle: Mix up the order of the items in a list.
terms.Vector3: Three numbers (X, Y, Z) for a position or direction in 3D.

examples.title: Roll a dice and pick a random prize
examples.code:
local rng = Random.new() -- a surprise seed each server

-- Roll a 6-sided dice
local roll = rng:NextInteger(1, 6)
print("You rolled a", roll)

-- Pick a random prize from a list
local prizes = { "Sword", "Shield", "Potion", "Hat" }
local prize = prizes[rng:NextInteger(1, #prizes)]
print("You won a", prize)

-- A random decimal between 0.5 and 2 for a size
local size = rng:NextNumber(0.5, 2)
print("Random size:", size)
explain: Random.new() with no seed gives different results each time the game runs.
NextInteger(1, 6) gives a whole number from 1 to 6, and both 1 and 6 are possible.
#prizes is how many items are in the list (4), so we pick a random spot from 1 to 4.

examples.title: Same seed, same results
examples.code:
local a = Random.new(42)
local b = Random.new(42)

print(a:NextInteger(1, 100), b:NextInteger(1, 100)) -- the same two numbers
print(a:NextInteger(1, 100), b:NextInteger(1, 100)) -- the same again
explain: Because they follow the same recipe, they give the same numbers in the same order.
This is how games can rebuild the exact same random world from one saved seed.

gotchas: Do not make a new Random.new() every time you need a number. Make one and keep using it.
Seeds are rounded toward zero, so seeds 0 and 0.99 give the same results.
Shuffle only works on lists without gaps (no nil holes in the middle). It changes the list itself and returns nothing.

Random.new.simple: Makes a new random number machine. With no seed, Roblox picks a surprise starting point. With a seed number, you get the same results every time for that seed.
Random.new.example:
local surprise = Random.new()  -- different every time
local repeatable = Random.new(12345) -- same every time
Random.new.gotcha: Decimal seeds are cut down to whole numbers, so 7 and 7.9 are the same seed.

Random:NextInteger.simple: Gives a random whole number from min to max, and both ends can come up. If you accidentally give the bigger number first, it swaps them for you.
Random:NextInteger.example:
local rng = Random.new()
local dice = rng:NextInteger(1, 6) -- 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, or 6
print(dice)

Random:NextNumber.simple: Gives a random decimal number. With no arguments it is between 0 and 1. With min and max, it is between those two.
Random:NextNumber.example:
local rng = Random.new()
print(rng:NextNumber())        -- like 0.4821
print(rng:NextNumber(10, 20))  -- like 13.77

Random:Shuffle.simple: Mixes up the order of a list, right in place (the list itself is changed). Every order is equally likely.
Random:Shuffle.example:
local rng = Random.new()
local games = { "Obby", "Race", "Tag", "Hide and Seek" }
rng:Shuffle(games)
print(table.concat(games, ", ")) -- a new random order
Random:Shuffle.gotcha: The list must not have nil gaps in the middle, or it errors. It returns nothing, so do not write `games = rng:Shuffle(games)`.

Random:NextUnitVector.simple: Gives a random direction as a Vector3 arrow of length 1. Every direction in 3D is equally likely. Multiply it to make it longer.
Random:NextUnitVector.example:
local rng = Random.new()
local direction = rng:NextUnitVector()
-- A random spot 10 studs away from the center
local spot = Vector3.new(0, 10, 0) + direction * 10
print(spot)

Random:Clone.simple: Makes a copy of this random machine at exactly the same point in its recipe. From then on, both give the same next numbers, but using one does not change the other.
Random:Clone.example:
local rng = Random.new(7)
local copy = rng:Clone()
print(rng:NextInteger(1, 100) == copy:NextInteger(1, 100)) --> true
